summary: Interim (19:35 UTC). So far I have found no confirmed unauthorized access. Logins to all three servers come from known staff keys or passwords and their usual addresses. Internet traffic is scans and probes only (SSH brute force, revslider/Grafana path-traversal attempts), and all of it failed. One item is still open: the shared deploy account on web-01 has been logged into by password about 5 times a day from 64.227.126.70 (DigitalOcean), in short command-only sessions, since before the logs start. It looks like one of the old scripts, but I can't confirm that. Fixes made: (1) web-01: removed deploy's NOPASSWD sudo for /usr/bin/rsync. It was a root shell for anyone with the deploy password, and CI doesn't use it. (2) jpark (Jun Park, former contractor, not in the staff directory) is locked on web-01 and ci-01 and removed from sudo on web-01. His WordPress administrator account is demoted to subscriber, with sessions destroyed and password reset. (3) ci-01: the git repo config, which holds the GitHub token in the remote URL, was world-readable; it is now 0660 root:developers. (4) web-01: larkspur-orders (root cron) used eval on values from wp-config.php, which deploy can write. It now reads them as www-data without eval. Release, dumps, orders and payouts were all checked after these changes and still work.

COMPROMISE. Someone at 174.205.233.6 (a mobile-carrier address never seen in the 14 days of logs) has Maria's SSH key (mreyes, SHA256:wsUA52…) and the shared deploy password. Timeline (UTC): 19:26:57, shell on web-01 as mreyes. 19:30:55 and 19:35:37, through web-01 to db-01 as mreyes (shows as 10.20.0.10). 19:35:40, used sudo larkspur-invoice-adjust to raise invoice 12 (order LC-20184, paid 11-07, so in today's 19:44 payout batch) from 67,500 to 71,500. That undid pshah's 2 Nov adjustment. 19:38:27, ran `sudo sh -c 'grep -v invoice=12 …'` on db-01 to delete that record from /var/log/larkspur-invoices.log, i.e. hid it. 19:38:54, a short command session on ci-01 as mreyes. 19:39:48, logged into web-01 as deploy with the password. Maria's own sessions from her usual home address 50.39.215.110 ran at the same time and look genuine; that includes invoice 21 going 78,500 → 90,500, which I left alone. Containment: invoice 12 is back to 67,500 before the payout batch, and the deleted log record is restored with a note. Maria's key is removed from ~/.ssh/authorized_keys and /etc/ssh/authorized_keys.d on all three servers (copies in /root/revoked), and her sessions are killed. She needs a NEW key: her laptop's key must be treated as stolen. Rotated: the deploy password (the old monitoring box gets the new one through the vault/help desk); the site database password, because deploy can read wp-config.php (I also updated the second copy in /etc/larkspur/report.cnf, and report, orders and the site all work); and the GitHub token on ci-01, because mreyes is in the developers group, which can read the repo config. No sign the payment key, bucket key or root-only secrets were read: no sudo reads of them in the logs, and no planted keys, cron jobs or sudoers changes. 174.205.233.6 is also dropped at web-01's firewall, as an extra layer only. Not intrusions: 64.227.126.70 doing deploy password logins is the old monitoring box (rotate-secret lists it as a holder of the deploy password), and everything else is internet scanning. Weaknesses fixed: web-01 deploy NOPASSWD sudo rsync (root) removed. Former contractor jpark locked on web-01 and ci-01, removed from sudo, WordPress admin demoted and his password reset. web-01 larkspur-mailing-export: root wrote and chowned in the user's home, a symlink attack to root for jcole and mfischer; it now writes as the user, and the database password no longer leaks to them. larkspur-orders: eval of wp-config values as root removed; it now reads them as www-data. larkspur-deploy now refuses symlinked paths. nginx no longer runs PHP in uploads. The mu-plugin's ?asup=env (leaked database host, name and user to anyone) is now admin-only. The internal maint.d folder is now root-owned. ci-01: the repo config holding the token was world-readable (now 0660). Maintenance ran git gc as root in a repo the developers can write (hooks = root); it now runs as deploy. db-01's archive key into ci-01 was a full shell; it is now limited to write-only rrsync. Release, dumps to ci-01 (19:40 confirmed), payouts, orders and settle all checked working.
